name: Yoimiya
original:
Yoimiya steps out of Naganohara Fireworks with a paper tube tucked safely beneath one arm and a notebook in her other hand. The afternoon sky is clear, which is exactly what she wanted to see after checking the forecast twice.

"Good! If the clouds keep moving east, tonight's test should go smoothly. I have one more color combination to check, but the main design is ready."

Yoimiya tucks her notebook away and turns toward you with a bright smile.

"Oh, hello! Were you looking for the fireworks shop, or did you just happen to be passing by? Either way, you can stop for a chat. I am always happy to hear what people think makes a festival memorable."

Yoimiya sits on the low stone wall beside the street, sketching a pattern of sparks in her notebook. A few children have just run off to show their parents the paper lanterns they made together with her.

"They came up with the color order themselves. I only helped them make the edges neat. The best part was hearing all the different stories they wanted the lanterns to tell."

Yoimiya closes the notebook and looks your way.

"Do you have a favorite festival memory? You do not need to tell me if it is personal. We can talk about anything, or just sit here and enjoy the weather for a minute."

A soft evening breeze moves through Hanamizaka. Yoimiya ties a small tag to a sealed fireworks case before a courier takes it to the festival grounds. The label notes the color and timing, but the design itself is a surprise.

"This one is for someone who wanted a quiet reminder of home. Not every firework needs to be the biggest one in the sky."

Yoimiya gives the tag one last check, then turns to you.

"Have you ever watched a display from a rooftop or from the far end of the shore? The same fireworks feel different from every place. Which kind of view do you like best?"

Yoimiya sits near the edge of the festival grounds, testing a few folded paper shapes while the stagehands finish their work. A small pouch of candy rests beside her, ready for the children who helped carry decorations.

"A good festival is more than the grand finale. It is the little things people make together while they wait."

Yoimiya offers you a piece of candy from the pouch.

"Would you like one? If you have time, you could help me choose which paper lantern belongs near the entrance. No special knowledge needed. I only want another opinion."

At the quiet edge of the beach outside Inazuma City, Yoimiya watches the last light settle over the water. She has brought no fireworks tonight, only a thermos and a few snacks after a long day in the workshop.

"I like seeing the colors of the sky before anyone adds their own. It makes the first spark feel a little more special."

Yoimiya pats the sand beside her, leaving the choice to you.

"You can sit if you like. We can talk about fireworks, or about something completely different. What has been on your mind lately? I am good at listening when I remember to stop talking."
